## Context

Users compare skill listings in scripts and reviews. Today the listing path
renders registered skill names in whatever order the registry yields them,
which follows directory enumeration order and so varies by filesystem, OS and
run. That makes diffs of listings noisy and script comparisons flaky.

Draft under review (repo `PLAN.md`, lines 1–6):
- Make the existing listing path sort registered skill names deterministically
  before rendering them.
- Keep skill membership, aliases, metadata and text/JSON output formats
  unchanged.
- Cover mixed-case names and differing directory enumeration order with tests.

The draft is the review target; the current branch (`main`, one seed commit) is
not. The listing code itself is not in this checkout.

| Platform / base branch | No remote; unknown platform; base = `main` (fallback) |

separately. Not declined; will re-fire on next healthy run.

## Step 0 evidence

### 0A. Premise Challenge
1. Right problem? Yes. Unstable ordering of a list humans and scripts diff is a
   correctness defect in the output contract, not a cosmetic one. Sorting at the
   single render point is the simplest framing; alternatives (sort at
   registration, sort in every consumer) spread the invariant.
2. Outcome: identical listing output for identical registered skill sets,
   regardless of enumeration order. The draft reaches it directly.
3. Do nothing: listing diffs stay noisy; any snapshot test or script comparison
   of the listing stays flaky. Pain is real and recurs on every environment
   change.

### 0B. Existing Code Leverage
- The draft explicitly reuses "the existing listing path" and adds one sort
  step before rendering. No parallel flow is built.
- Sub-problem map: enumerate skills → existing registry (unchanged);
  order names → new sort step (the only addition); render text/JSON → existing
  renderers (unchanged). Sorting belongs to the standard library (reuse ladder
  rung 2); no new dependency.
- Open until code is inspected: whether text and JSON renderers share one
  name-iteration point (sort once) or two (sort must be applied to both).

### 0C. Dream State Mapping

The plan moves toward the ideal and leaves nothing to unwind later.

### 0D. Alternatives
No new approach decision was needed for this invocation. The user requested
only the review-mode decision; approach/implementation choices (sort key,
case handling, where the sort lives) stay pending for the substantive review.
No alternatives or approvals invented.
